newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says will hit tough Maastricht deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: Italy says will hit tough Maastricht deficit goal.

text.p: Italy's Treasury undersecretary Laura Pennacchi said on Tuesday that the country's 1997 deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) ratio is expected to be three percent using the definition applied in the Maastricht Treaty.
Italy traditionally uses a different definition of the ratio, which they have already said will touch the crucial three percent level next year.

However analysts said that according to the stricter 'public administration' calculation of deficit, demanded by Maastricht for founder members of the single European currency, Italy's deficit/GDP ratio next year would be nearer to four percent.

"If the economy's performance is in line with our forecast the public administration deficit will be three percent of GDP", she told reporters at a briefing on the 1997 budget approved by cabinet last Friday.

The public administration calculation in Italy adds some 20 trillion lire, or 0.9 percent of GDP, to the deficit by including tax rebates owed by the government to companies along with back payments due to certain catagories of pensioners.
However a treasury source indicated that Italy would be within its rights to include this sum in the overall debt mountain and not the annual deficit figure.
The money owed to companies and pensioners does not necessarily have to be paid back in 1997.

EMU founder members have to cut the ratio between their annual budget deficit and GDP to no more than three percent by the end of 1997 to join the single currency set to start in 1999. Rome newsroom 39-6-6782501
